observation.visible_scene: A stylized 3D render of faceted gemstones set against a bright, near-white background. A central cluster of three in-focus stones persists throughout: a deep-blue faceted gem on the left, a colorless/white cut diamond at top-center, and a round pink-red gem on the right. These are framed by larger, heavily blurred gem shapes in the background (blue upper-left, clear upper-right, red lower-left, clear lower-right).
visible_changes: The blue gem visibly rotates in place: its crown tilts from pointing up-and-left in the first frames toward a more upright, vertically elongated orientation by the last frames, altering its silhouette and the facet pattern shown.
The pink gem's facet pattern and apparent tilt shift gradually, and it drifts slightly rightward relative to the white gem while keeping its round outline.
The white gem remains near top-center but changes scale/position modestly as the viewpoint moves.

The blurred background gems translate relative to the central cluster (parallax): the lower-left red mass enlarges and slides toward the left edge, and the upper-right clear shape shifts toward center, indicating a slow camera orbit/dolly rather than the foreground stones traveling across the scene.

Star-shaped sparkle glints appear and vanish on the pink and blue gems at different moments (concentrated on the pink stone early, on the blue stone later), an animated highlight effect independent of the stones' motion.
The overall framing subtly tightens and re-centers the three-stone cluster over the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the stones' rotation is a continuous spin or an oscillation, and what precedes or follows the cropped segment.
What produces the sparkle glints (light-source movement vs rendered highlight animation).
The full arrangement of gems beyond the visible frame.
uncertain_details: The camera path (orbit vs zoom vs both) cannot be cleanly separated from the stones' own rotation, since both change apparent positions.
It is unclear whether the white gem rotates independently or only appears to shift due to viewpoint change.
Distinguishing true reflections/ghosts from the separate blurred background gem shapes is not fully determinable.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
